summary: Shares the latest ARPANET maps, both geographic and logical, together with a list of Hosts connected. The maps show IMPs and TIPs and the status of the computers on the net as of mid-December 1973.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC describes two ARPANET maps and lists hosts connected to the network. The list also includes some sites expected to join later.

questions: what is a very distant host
subtitle: A December 1973 snapshot of ARPANET maps, host names and connection status.

tldr.problem: Readers needed a dated record of ARPANET connections and of the hosts attached to the network.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes a geographic map, a logical map, and a list of current and planned hosts with addresses, names, computers and status.
tldr.outcome: The maps are omitted from this copy. The unit metadata says RFC 603 later updated this snapshot.

today: RFC 597 is a dated snapshot with status listed as Unknown. The unit metadata says it was updated by RFC 603.

sections.title: What the Maps Show
sections.content:
The geographic map shows all IMPs and TIPs then installed in the subnetwork. The logical map records the status of computers as of December 10, 1973, with MIT-MULTICS shown attached to IMP 44 rather than IMP 5.

On the logical map, intersecting ovals mark hosts with subnet interfaces, a small v marks a Very Distant Host interface, solid circles are IMPs and circles containing T are TIPs. Two jagged lines mark satellite links. The map's names are unofficial IMP names, not official host names. The maps themselves are omitted from this copy.
sections.plainLanguage: One map shows where network equipment is located. The other shows how computers connect, using different shapes for hosts, IMPs and TIPs.

sections.title: The Host List
sections.content:
The host list includes current sites and sites projected to join within the next two months. An incomplete list of later installations appears at the end. Each host's network address is shown in octal and decimal, and subnet interfaces appear in parentheses.

A site calls itself a Server or User. A limited Server restricts the group of users, while a dedicated Server restricts the kind of service. The status column can also name a special operating system not supplied by the computer manufacturer.
sections.plainLanguage: The list gives each host's address, official name, computer and reported role. Some entries describe planned connections rather than current ones.

sections.title: Official Host Names
sections.content:
This RFC contains the official host names as of December 1973. The RFC says Jake Feinler at the NIC will maintain naming conventions and an official host-name list.

The list was to be published in ARPANEWS, made available online through the NIC, and issued periodically in the Resource Notebook. Other sites are encouraged to make copies available on their own systems.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC identifies the official names for that period. It says the NIC will maintain and distribute the name list.
